Bring your own key

Use your own provider keys through the router: your key stays yours, and the fee is a line you can see.

A workspace can store its own provider keys and route through them. The router uses your key to call the provider; the provider bills you directly, and the model price is not added to your balance.

What the router keeps

The router charges a request fee on traffic that runs on your own key or your own model. The rule, as built (PRICE-2):

  • The fee is a separate line of the usage ledger, never folded into a price.
  • A free allowance of requests per month comes first. The allowance is a count over the sealed ledger for the calendar month in UTC, so it starts again each month and cannot be overspent by a retry.
  • A request counts once: a retried request is not charged twice.
  • Traffic that runs on the platform's own accounts carries no request fee; it carries the model price.
  • A trial plan carries no request fee.

The amounts, the allowance and the period are plan data. The usage page shows them before anything is charged, and the doors under the Credits and usage chapter show what was charged.

Custody

The custody entry on each model of GET /v1/models says whose key pays the provider for that route. A provider key is a credential object of the workspace: it is never shown again after it is stored and never printed in a log.

Signing in to a provider instead of pasting a key is coming (BYOK-OAUTH-1).
